questions.q: Why does Meridian's design make Entra ID the single policy decision point instead of letting on-prem Active Directory keep authenticating clinic workstations directly?
options: So every sign-in, on-prem or cloud, is evaluated by one policy engine instead of two separate systems making inconsistent decisions
Because Active Directory cannot run alongside Entra ID at all
Because MediCore requires a cloud-only identity provider to function
To remove the need for multi-factor authentication
questions.explain: Two identity systems making independent access decisions is exactly the gap a single policy decision point closes.

questions.q: In the Conditional Access policy shown, what does enabling continuous access evaluation add beyond a normal sign-in check?
options: It disables MFA for trusted networks
It lets a session be re-evaluated mid-stream against new risk signals, not just checked once at login
It automatically renews the user's password
It only applies to guest accounts
questions.explain: Continuous access evaluation is explicit verification extended across the life of a session, not a one-time login-time check.

questions.q: What replaced VPN-based access to Clinical Systems in this design?
options: A shared service account with a static password
Nothing -- VPN access was kept unchanged
A software-defined perimeter broker that evaluates identity and device signals per request
A firewall rule allowing all internal traffic
questions.explain: The broker checks the same identity and device signals on every request, instead of a VPN tunnel granting broad reachability for a whole session.

questions.q: Why does blocking workstation-to-workstation SMB and RDP across segment boundaries matter, even if a Conditional Access policy elsewhere fails?
options: It has no real security effect -- it's purely cosmetic
It only affects guest accounts, not staff
It replaces the need for device compliance checks entirely
It limits blast radius by removing the network path a compromised device would need to move laterally into another segment
questions.explain: Assume-breach design accepts one control can fail and still limits damage by cutting off the lateral-movement path itself.

questions.q: What makes the workload identity token issued to the ClaimFlow billing vendor different from a typical long-lived API key?
options: It is scoped to exactly one action (claims:submit) and expires in fifteen minutes
It grants unrestricted access to every MediCore endpoint
It never expires once issued
It is shared across every vendor Meridian works with
questions.explain: A workload identity token scoped tightly and expiring quickly is what keeps a vendor integration from becoming a standing broad-access credential.
